question: Does API-assisted collection produce a better learned initialization than strong ReAct self-collection under matched training exposure?

collection.api: Original JSON actor + cached public-reset-only strategy, first four turns
collection.react: Two fixed public task-family examples + think/action, no teacher card

target_view: Public initial observation + last 12 non-thought action/observation pairs; canonical JSON action labels. Remove all cards, examples and thoughts.

matching.action_count: minimum eligible count per pair; evenly spaced
matching.exclusions: invalid format, thoughts, literal Nothing happens targets, overlength; retain failed physical actions in history

b_training.parameterization: Frozen A + fresh B LoRA. Tests additive adaptation, not unrestricted same-parameter plasticity.

evaluation.A_retention: JSON at 0 and 128; ReAct at A start only. Shared A start evaluated once on cool branch.

primary: API minus ReAct: equal-weight cool/heat mean normalized raw success AUC under common JSON execution
secondary: Initial success, endpoint success, baseline-subtracted gain AUC
Per-family curves; heat within-family versus cool A-unseen family
Common ReAct execution at B start/end
Source collection yield and real input/output costs
inference: Paired crossed bootstrap of 3 training-seed indices and task groups within each family, 4000 draws; preserve seed pairing across families

demonstration_audit.rule: Public goal plus visible numbered receptacle multiset

limitations: Reused exploratory query tasks, not new confirmation evidence
Equal samples/updates do not imply identical target/input token FLOPs
The two collection harnesses differ in examples and action interface; this is a pipeline comparison, not an isolated card effect
ReAct evaluation supplies cool demonstrations; label this few-shot execution, not zero-shot goal transfer
Frozen A plus B and three seeds cannot establish pure plasticity or RSI
BF16 batching can change trajectories despite paired request RNG
